sources.execution_note: The 2015 C# example subscribes minute data and evaluates daily indicators once per day; a daily next-open backtest is an execution adaptation.

sources.author: Daniel Rodriguez

exact_signal_rules.sizing: not specified in the strategy class

version_specific_equality_rules.2015_source: Upward crossing requires immediately previous fast < slow and current fast > slow; downward crossing uses the opposite strict inequalities. An equality bar breaks the crossing.
version_specific_equality_rules.current_source: Crossing remembers the last nonzero fast-minus-slow difference across equality bars. This is a later tie-handling change.

sources.chronology_note: Official strategy and corresponding strict previous-bar crossover helper both retrieved from the history commit dated 2015-08-16. Do not attribute the modern nonzero-difference tie handling to this older snapshot.
sources.performance_claim: No profitability claim inferred from the source example.

sources.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation

document_dates.journal_publication_stated_in_pdf: Spring 2007, The Journal of Wealth Management

sources.source_type: Original paper text obtained from an unaffiliated public GitHub mirror

mirror_source.content_identity: PDF identifies Mebane T. Faber, February 2013 update, SSRN abstract 962461

exact_signal_rules.frequency: last trading day of each month; ignore intramonth signal changes
exact_signal_rules.indicator: 10-month simple average of total-return month-end observations, including the just-completed current month and nine previous months
exact_signal_rules.equality: neither rule fires; retain previous position
exact_signal_rules.allocation: each asset-class sleeve equally weighted at 20 percent, independently long or cash

sources.chronology_note: The mirrored document identifies the simple rule as the 2006/2007 model and a February 2013 update. Publisher/author original bodies were inaccessible in this environment, so provenance is weaker than for official code.
sources.performance_claim: Paper claims are not treated as our independently verified returns.

study_adaptations_to_disclose: Signals observed only on a completed daily/monthly bar, with entry/exit at a later executable price instead of assuming a known closing price can be traded at that same close.
A fixed 3 * ATR(14) protective stop, risk budgeting and position caps are our 2026 research overlay; none of the three source models specifies this stop.
Five available ETF proxies, costs, zero-interest cash and any prop-rule replay are not the original paper portfolio or a verified executable CFD/futures contract.
Modern equality handling must remain the policy explicitly frozen before price retrieval; it cannot be changed after seeing results.

A dated source rule and protocol frozen before our fetch reduce our own parameter selection; retrospective market history remains visible to source authors and does not constitute prospective live proof.

access_limitations.original_host_attempts: AQR, its image host, author Meb Faber, SSRN, Yale, Duke and Oxford requests were rejected by the network proxy with CONNECT HTTP 403. Narrow source domains were saved in the environment draft, but saving does not apply network configuration and actual requests still failed.
access_limitations.fallback: No paper numbers or rule excerpts are asserted to have been retrieved from blocked primary hosts. Faber is explicitly a mirror; the two official algorithm projects were actually retrieved on immutable GitHub commit URLs.
